quotes.text:
Why I built Aegis AI

A couple of years ago my phone became my biggest enemy. I would sit down to work, open Instagram for “a minute,” and surface two hours later. The deeper I dug, the worse the research looked:

•Stanford MRI studies show gray-matter shrinkage in the prefrontal cortex from chronic screen time.

•Constant digital interruption can cut measured IQ by roughly ten points—more than moderate cannabis use.

•Adults 18-25 already show measurable cortical thinning.

The average person now burns six hours a day on low-quality content. Oxford’s 2024 “word of the year”, brain rot - captures it.

How the app tries to break the loop

•Personalised AI coach – identifies your worst offenders and proposes a blocking schedule reviewed each week.

•Pre-emptive prompts – breathing drills or short quotations pop up when you try to open a blocked app.

•Adaptive limits – rules tighten or relax based on actual behaviour.

•Circadian sync – mornings and nights get stricter blocks to protect REM and deep focus.

•Deep focus sessions – structured sprints that keep everything else silenced.

Early results

Beta users report two to three reclaimed hours a day and a noticeable drop in “phantom” notification checking.

Free trial for HN

HN readers can run a full AI screen-time diagnosis and a three-day trial with code "HCKR".

I would love blunt feedback on the previously mentioned points and in general to make this the ultimate screen time and digital wellbeing app.
